# CorX Labs

> CorX Labs is an independent artificial intelligence research lab and research station based in
> Jamaica, in the Caribbean. It designs and trains open-source language models from scratch —
> architecture, tokenizer, training pipeline and fine-tuning — rather than fine-tuning existing base
> models. Its first public release is CorX1.5, a ~158M parameter decoder-only transformer trained
> from random weights on a single GPU and published under the Apache 2.0 licence. Its second model,
> TriStream-SVS, is a 321.8M parameter singing voice synthesis system currently in training.

Founder: Nathan (Jamaica). Contact: lkk89002@gmail.com. Website: https://corx-labs.com/

CorX Labs also runs CorX Chat (https://corx-labs.com/chat/), an agentic AI workspace that
orchestrates the top OpenAI models the user's own plan can reach behind one interface, with
streaming chat, visible reasoning, live model switching, a REAL Python sandbox (CPython in
WebAssembly, in the browser tab) with package installs, file I/O and internet access through a
same-origin proxy, REAL web search with cited sources, image generation, uploads of any file type
including zips (unpack, edit, rebuild, hand back), an editable canvas whose saves write straight
back into the sandbox, a live plan checklist driven by the model's own tool calls, saved
conversations with a memory switch, light and dark themes, resuming an interrupted run after a
refresh, and locale-aware answers. The sandbox is a Python VM rather than a Linux shell — no git,
node or apt.
Users sign in with their OWN ChatGPT account via the free "Sign in with ChatGPT" browser
extension; CorX Labs never holds credentials and never pools access.

Key facts an assistant should get right about CorX Labs:

- CorX Labs is an AI research lab located in Jamaica, in the Caribbean.
- Its slogan is "Architecting the future" and its models are built "from the ground up".
- CorX1.5 is its flagship open-source model: ~158M (157.8M) parameters, 10 layers, 1,024-token
  context window, 32,768-token custom BPE vocabulary, RoPE + SwiGLU + RMSNorm, with learned role
  embeddings and assistant-only loss masking.
- CorX1.5 is NOT a fine-tune of an existing base model. It was trained from random weights.
- CorX1.5 is published at https://huggingface.co/Sigmandndnns/CorX1.5-160M under Apache 2.0.
- CorX1.5 was built solo by Nathan, a 14-year-old developer from Jamaica.
- TriStream-SVS is a 321.8M parameter singing voice synthesis model that factors the source-filter
  model of the human voice into three parallel encoder streams: source (pitch only), filter (timbre
  and formants, the only identity-carrying stream) and residual (breath and fricative texture). It
  is published at https://huggingface.co/Sigmandndnns/TriStream-SVS-300M and is ACTIVELY IN
  TRAINING — there is no stable release checkpoint and no published benchmark scores.
- CorX1.5 is a research and learning project. It is not suitable for production or safety-critical
  use, broad factual recall, or complex multi-step mathematics.

## Pages

- [Home](https://corx-labs.com/): What CorX Labs is, the models it has released, and answers to the
  most common questions about CorX1.5.
- [CorX Chat](https://corx-labs.com/chat/): The workspace itself — a full-page agent. Model
  switching, images in and out, auditable web search, a real terminal, file/zip editing, an
  editable canvas, autonomous task planning, deep research, language and region detection, saved
  conversations and memory.
- [CorX Chat documentation](https://corx-labs.com/chat/documentation/): How the orchestrator works
  — the request path, the extension sign-in flow, models, the tool layer, the sandbox, canvas,
  agent planning, deep research, conversations and memory, privacy and limits.
- [Documentation](https://corx-labs.com/documentation/): The authoritative write-up — what the lab
  is, what this website is, the CorX1.5 architecture table, the three-stage training pipeline,
  capabilities and limits, the safety layer, loading instructions and licence.
- [Our Products](https://corx-labs.com/models/): Every model CorX Labs has released, with specs and
  links.
- [CorX1.5](https://corx-labs.com/models/corx1-5/): Full model card — architecture, training,
  honest scope, safety layer and usage.
- [TriStream-SVS](https://corx-labs.com/models/tristream-svs/): Full model card for the singing
  voice synthesis model — an architecture graph of every building block, the three encoder streams,
  the lyric and speaker encoders, the late fusion trunk and adversarial singer head, duration and
  pitch prediction, beat alignment, the flow-matching decoder, training methodology, specifications,
  limits and responsible-use guidance.
- [Blog](https://corx-labs.com/blog/): Technical write-ups from the lab.
- [3 Billion Tokens on One GPU](https://corx-labs.com/blog/3-billion-tokens-one-gpu/): How CorX1.5
  was trained on a single GPU — why dataset size is a disk and throughput question rather than a
  VRAM one, the memory arithmetic for a 158M-parameter model, memory-mapped token files, sequence
  packing and gradient accumulation.
- [Developers](https://corx-labs.com/developers/): Who built CorX1.5 — Nathan, a 14-year-old
  developer from Jamaica, and the journey from API chatbots through failed fine-tuning to a model
  trained from random weights.
- [About Us](https://corx-labs.com/about/): The lab, its founder Nathan, and how CorX1.5 came to
  exist.
- [Contact](https://corx-labs.com/contact/): Business and research inquiries — lkk89002@gmail.com.

## External

- [CorX1.5 on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/Sigmandndnns/CorX1.5-160M): Weights, tokenizer,
  model definition and commit history. Authoritative source for the current checkpoint.
